claims.text: Adding 5 wt% tungsten will increase yield strength at 1000°C by 20% relative to the tungsten-free baseline alloy.
Adding 5 wt% tungsten will limit the density increase to 1% relative to the baseline alloy.
Adding 5 wt% tungsten will preserve room-temperature mechanical performance.
Tungsten addition stabilizes the body-centered cubic phase.
BCC-phase stabilization and solid-solution strengthening caused by tungsten produce the predicted high-temperature yield-strength improvement.
The proposed intervention is the addition of 5 wt% tungsten to an otherwise unspecified refractory high-entropy alloy.
The material is evaluated in the as-cast state.
The primary test condition is 1000°C under a stated tensile stress of 500 MPa.
The hypothesis is expected to hold from 900°C to 1100°C and over a loading range of 400–600 MPa.
Temperatures of 900–1100°C and loads of 400–600 MPa are typical operating conditions for jet-turbine applications.
Composition and processing variation may affect the outcome.
Yield-strength measurements may have approximately ±5% uncertainty.
The hypothesis is falsified if the tungsten-containing alloy has less than a 15% yield-strength improvement or more than a 2% density increase.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis promises a density increase limited to 1%, but the experiment only falsifies it when the increase exceeds 2%; results between 1% and 2% violate the stated hypothesis without triggering falsification.
The hypothesis requires preservation of room-temperature performance, but the proposed experiment includes no room-temperature mechanical measurement or corresponding falsification criterion.
